questions.question: At what rate of compound interest per annum, a sum of Rs. 20000 becomes Rs. 23152.50 in 1 year 6 months compounded half-yearly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Amount** to **Principal** for 3 half-years = 23152.50 : 20000 = 9261 : 8000

For 1 half-year, take the cube root: ³√9261 : ³√8000 = 21 : 20

**Half-yearly Rate** = (21 − 20)/20 × 100 = 5%

**Annual Rate** = 5% × 2 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10% per annum.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹20000

**Amount (A)** = ₹23152.50

**Time (t)** = 1 year 6 months = 1.5 years

**Compounding:** Half-yearly

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6fcaa1b059d399639d3e94ed37395e92d996de517b56bc04a22370cf7e42c18.png] 

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where r = **half-yearly rate** and n = **number of half-years**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ n = 1.5 × 2 = 3 periods

⇒ 23152.50 = 20000(1 + r/100)³

⇒ 23152.50 / 20000 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ 231525 / 200000 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ 9261 / 8000 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ (21 / 20)³ = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ 21 / 20 = 1 + r/100

⇒ r / 100 = 21/20 − 1 = 1 / 20

⇒ r = 100 / 20 = 5% (Half-yearly rate)

⇒ **Annual Rate** = 2 × r = 2 × 5% = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10% per annum.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-yearly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual **rate** is divided by 2 (r = R/2) and the **time** is multiplied by 2 (n = 2 × T).

Quarterly Compounding

For quarterly compounding, the rate is divided by 4 (r = R/4) and the number of periods is n = 4 × T.

Effective Rate of Interest

The **effective rate** for two periods of r% is given by the successive formula: r + r + (r × r)/100.

questions.question: ​If p : q is 4 : 3 and q : r is 5 : 2. Find p : q : r.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To combine two ratios p : q and q : r, use the direct cross-multiplication (inverted N) method.

Given, p : q = 4 : 3 and q : r = 5 : 2

p : q : r = (4 × 5) : (3 × 5) : (3 × 2)

p : q : r = 20 : 15 : 6

**∴ The correct answer is 20 : 15 : 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

p : q = 4 : 3

q : r = 5 : 2

**Method Used:**

Equalise the common term 'q' in both ratios by taking the LCM of its respective values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50686c34a9161ad3696b3194b5fea0dfada7410355173ff90457ce7e1098f675.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM of the 'q' terms (3 and 5) = 15

⇒ Multiply the first ratio by 5 to make q = 15.

⇒ p : q = (4 × 5) : (3 × 5) = 20 : 15

⇒ Multiply the second ratio by 3 to make q = 15.

⇒ q : r = (5 × 3) : (2 × 3) = 15 : 6

⇒ Since 'q' is now equal in both ratios, combine them directly.

⇒ p : q : r = 20 : 15 : 6

**∴ The correct answer is 20 : 15 : 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two individual ratios a : b and c : d is defined as ac : bd. It is computed by multiplying the antecedents together and the consequents together.

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of any given ratio a : b is given by squaring its terms, resulting in a² : b².

Proportion

When two ratios are strictly equal (a : b = c : d), they form a proportion. In any standard proportion, the product of the extremes is always equal to the product of the means (a × d = b × c).

questions.question: The two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are 12 cm and 5 cm respectively. If one of the diagonals is 13 cm long, then what is the area of the parallelogram?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Observe that the sides **5 cm**, **12 cm**, and **13 cm** form a **Pythagorean triplet** because 5² + 12² = 13².

This means the **diagonal** and the two **adjacent sides** form a **right-angled triangle**.

A parallelogram is a **rectangle** when its sides satisfy the Pythagorean theorem with the diagonal.

**Area of Parallelogram** = Product of adjacent sides = 12 × 5 = 60 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Adjacent sides **a = 12 cm**, **b = 5 cm**, and diagonal **d = 13 cm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/487979496d51df842d5a48d1fce7ca5ec4171b48245d4b7fea3086cf11d9369a.png] 

The diagonal of a **parallelogram** divides it into two **triangles** of equal area.

⇒ Area of **ΔABC** with sides 5, 12, and 13 can be found using **Heron's Formula**.

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (5 + 12 + 13) ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − d)]

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √[15(15 − 5)(15 − 12)(15 − 13)]

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √[15 × 10 × 3 × 2] = √900 = 30 cm²

⇒ **Area of Parallelogram** = 2 × Area of ΔABC = 2 × 30 = 60 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Parallelogram

The area is calculated as **Base × Height** or **ab sin(θ)**, where a and b are adjacent sides and θ is the included angle.

Parallelogram Law

For any parallelogram with sides a, b and diagonals d₁, d₂, the relation is **d₁² + d₂² = 2(a² + b²)**.

Properties of Diagonals

The diagonals of a **parallelogram** bisect each other, but they are equal in length only if the parallelogram is a **rectangle** or a **square**.</p

questions.question: There are 300 men in a group. They have food for 30 days. After 10 days, 100 more men join the group. Remaining food will last for how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining food duration for **300 men** = 30 − 10 = **20 days**.

Total men after 10 days = 300 + 100 = **400 men**.

Since food is constant, Men × Days = Constant ⇒ 300 × 20 = 400 × New Days.

New Days = 6000 ÷ 400 = **15 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of men (M₁) = **300**

Initial food duration = **30 days**

Time elapsed = **10 days**

Additional men joined = **100**

**Formula Used:**

M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ (where M is men and D is remaining days)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dcfc878157b6dcf0a7d5dee88d6fb45b89477bfaf83b565e29a473da17702df3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total **food units** initially = 300 × 30 = 9000 man-days.

⇒ Food **consumed** in 10 days = 300 × 10 = 3000 man-days.

⇒ **Remaining food** units = 9000 − 3000 = 6000 man-days.

⇒ Total **new men** (M₂) = 300 + 100 = 400.

⇒ Number of days food will last (D₂) = Remaining Food ÷ M₂

⇒ D₂ = 6000 ÷ 400

⇒ D₂ = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion in Time and Work

The number of days a provision lasts is **inversely proportional** to the number of people. If people increase, the days decrease: M₁/M₂ = D₂/D₁.

Chain Rule Formula

For problems involving men, days, and hours, use (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂, where W is the work or amount of food.

Remaining Provision Logic

Always calculate based on **remaining capacity**. If 'x' days have passed out of 'T' total days, the calculation becomes M₁ × (T − x) = M₂ × Dₙₑw.</p

questions.question: How many countries share the international land border with India, as of 2022?
questions.solution:

• India's geography is incredibly diverse. It includes:
 
 
• **The Himalayan Mountain Range: **In the north, it borders with the world's highest mountain range, which includes Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga, the world's highest and third highest peaks, respectively.
 
• **Northern Plains:** South of the Himalayas, there are fertile river plains, largely fed by rivers such as the Ganges, Yamuna, and Brahmaputra. These plains are densely populated and are the agricultural hub of the country.
 
• **Thar Desert: **To the west, in the state of Rajasthan and extending into Pakistan, is the arid Thar Desert.
 
• **Central Plateau:** Further south, there is the Deccan plateau, which is flanked by the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats, both of which are mountain ranges.
 
• **Coastal Plains:** On the western and eastern sides of the peninsula, there are narrow coastal plains that provide the country with a significant amount of coastline along the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, respectively.
 
• **Islands:** India also has several islands, the largest of which are Andaman and Nicobar in the Bay of Bengal and Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• These diverse geographical features contribute to India's rich biodiversity, with various ecosystems ranging from desert to rainforest, from high-altitude alpine conditions to fertile plains, and mangroves to coral reefs.

questions.question: Materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them are called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insulator**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulators: **
 
• Insulators are materials that do not allow the flow of electric current.
 
• **The electrons** in insulator materials are tightly bound to their atoms and do not move freely, thus preventing the flow of electric current.
 
• Examples of insulators include **rubber, glass, and most plastics.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conductors: **

 
 
• Conductors are materials that allow the flow of electric current.
 
• They have free electrons that can move easily between atoms.
 
• This movement of electrons is what we refer to as an electric current.
 
• Examples of good conductors include metals like copper, aluminum, and gold.
 
 
 
• **Capacitors:**
 
 
• Capacitors are not a type of material, but a type of component used in electronic circuits.
 
• A capacitor is a device that stores electrical energy in an electric field.
 
• It is made of two conductive plates separated by an insulator (also called a dielectric).
 
• When a voltage is applied across the plates, an electric field is created and energy is stored.
 
 
 
• **Inductors:**
 
 
• Like capacitors, inductors are also components used in electronic circuits, not a type of material.
 
• An inductor is a coil of wire that stores energy in a magnetic field when electric current flows through it.
 
• The property of an inductor to oppose a change in current is known as inductance.
 
• Inductors are often used in analog circuits and signal processing.

__
 
• **Plants** with green and tender stems are called herbs.
 
• **Herbs** are usually short, non-woody plants.
 
• They might be **annuals, biennials, or perennials, but the common feature is their soft, green, and tender stem structure.**
 
• Examples of herbs include **grasses, ferns, and certain types of flowering plants.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shrubs**:

 
 
• Shrubs are medium-sized, semi-woody plants.
 
• They are usually multi-stemmed, smaller than trees, and have a bushy appearance.
 
• Shrubs can be both evergreen or deciduous. Examples of shrubs include holly, rose, and azalea.
 
 
 
• **Trees: **
 
 
• Trees are tall, woody plants.
 
• They typically have a single main stem or trunk that grows to a considerable height and bear lateral branches.
 
• Examples include oaks, maples, and pines. They play a crucial role in producing oxygen and sequestering carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Canopy: **
 
 
• Canopy refers to the overhead layer or habitat formed by mature tree crowns in a forest.
 
• It's not a type of plant, but rather a term that describes a particular layer within a forest ecosystem.
 
• The canopy provides shelter and habitat to various animals and plants.
 
 
 
• **Herbs: **
 
 
• Herbs are small, non-woody plants.
 
• They have green and tender stems.
 
• They usually die back to the ground at the end of each growing season.
 
• They can be annuals (life cycle completed in one growing season), biennials (life cycle completed in two growing seasons), or perennials (live for several to many growing seasons).
 
• Examples of herbs include basil, mint, and dill.
